input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
errors: First digitiser pass let frame ticks, marker strokes and a legend sample line into the dashed-curve series, and dropped the EUT sigma curve, which rises above the frame top; fixed by calibrating on the exact frames, dropping strokes near markers, and giving solid polylines extra padding (found from a smoothness check before the run).
A run of the full marine-hull suite with bare python3 -m pytest failed because the default python3 has no pytest; reran through pyenv.py.

doc_friction.issue: 7zd's edit to Threats to validity broke a sentence ('...exists here, and the solar km/day only as a resistance multiplier'), and check_numbers.py cannot catch prose breakage; fixed here.

says to use PY=$(python3 platform/ci/pyenv.py pytest ...) for tests, but this still cost one failed attempt: `python3 -m unittest discover` fails on marine-hull/tests because it has no __init__.py. A one-line 'run a project suite with $PY -m pytest -q <slug>/tests' would save it.

deviations.why: pick_track's CHAIN note (30 sub-steps of milestone 7) suggested a paper step. I chose a state-of-the-art baseline comparison instead, because the programme had no published-method baseline on its only in-range tank data, and that is a reviewer's first question.
deviations.did: Milestone 7ze compares against the four published curves, and also repairs one paper sentence.
deviations.result: The finding (our heave error ties the state of the art; A35 carries the overshoot) goes straight into section III-A of the paper.

notes: Programme marine-hull, milestone 7ze. Expectations were committed before the run (3ee5fe778). E1, E4 and E5 held; E2, E3 and E6 were refuted. Part D, added post hoc and marked as such, puts the heave overshoot in the A35/A53 added-mass coupling. Checks: check_numbers ok (146 claims), build.py ok, check_posts ok, check_md_links ok, cite_check ok, 18 new and affected tests pass; full marine-hull suite: 464 passed in 102 s (python3.13 via pyenv.py).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: digitising four curve families from vector PDFs, adding a coupling override to the strip code, a 6-expectation experiment, paper and post: about 1.5 days for a postdoc

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
